title: Tensor flatness of the closed-support quotient sheaf
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use ordinary sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], on small representatives of the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Derived categories are unbounded localizations at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] and a closed immersion $a:C\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose open complement $j:T\setminus C\hookrightarrow T$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], set
$$Q^	au_{T,C}=\operatorname{coker}(j_!\underline A_{T\setminus C}\longrightarrow\underline A_T),\qquad 	au=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet},$$
where the arrow is induced by inclusion of the open object into the final object and extension by zero is [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Denote the quotient map by $r^	au_{T,C}$. For both topologies, $Q^	au_{T,C}$ is flat: tensoring with it preserves short exact sequences [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Its complex concentrated in degree zero is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. In the etale topology its geometric stalk [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is canonically $A$ on $C$ and zero on $T\setminus C$, with the quotient generator mapping to $1$ on $C$. For $
u_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], the canonical comparison $
u_T^*Q^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}\cong Q^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}$ is the one taking $
u_T^*r^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}$ to $r^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: the support quotient has flat terms and its etale quotient pulls back to the pro-etale quotient.

proof.text: For the etale topology, apply the open-closed short exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] with $\Lambda=A$ to $F=\underline A_T$: $0\to j_!j^{-1}\underline A_T\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}\underline A_T\xrightarrow{\eta}a_*a^{-1}\underline A_T\to0$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](1), applied to $u=j$ and to $u=a$, the inverse images of the constant ring sheaf are canonically the constant ring sheaves $\underline A_{T\setminus C}$ and $\underline A_C$, the identifications carrying constant sections to the same scalars. The first arrow is the arrow defining $Q^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}$: by the free-Yoneda bijection [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] followed by the universal property of sheafification, a map $j_!\underline A_{T\setminus C}\to N$ is determined by the image of the generator $e_{\mathrm{id}}$ in $N(T\setminus C)$, because the presheaf of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] is $\underline A_T[h_{T\setminus C}]$ (an etale $V\to T$ has at most one map to $T\setminus C$). The counit $\varepsilon$ is the transpose of the identity of $j^{-1}\underline A_T$, so it sends the generator to $1|_{T\setminus C}$, and so does the arrow induced by the inclusion of the open object into the final object. Hence $Q^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}\cong a_*\underline A_C$ canonically, and under this isomorphism $r^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}$ is the unit $\eta$ followed by the identification of (1); it sends the constant section $1$ to the constant section $1$ of $\underline A_C$. For the pro-etale topology the same argument uses the ringed open-closed exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] for the ring sheaf $\underline A_T$, whose hypothesis is exactly the quasi-compactness of $j$ added to the statement: $0\to j_!j^{-1}\underline A_T\to\underline A_T\to a_*a^{-1}\underline A_T\to0$. Here $j^{-1}\underline A_T=\underline A_T|_{T\setminus C}=\underline A_{T\setminus C}$ by [def-weil-extension-by-zero], whose presheaf $P_M$ for $M=\underline A_{T\setminus C}$ is again $\underline A_T[h_{T\setminus C}]$, so the first arrow is again the defining arrow. The module pullback of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] gives $a^*\underline A_T=a^{-1}\underline A_T\otimes_{a^{-1}\underline A_T,c}\underline A_C\cong\underline A_C$. Thus $Q^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}\cong a_*\underline A_C$, with $r^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}$ the corresponding unit, again sending $1$ to $1$.

proof.text: The constant ring sheaf $\underline A_C$ is free of rank one as a module over itself, hence flat: $G\otimes_{\underline A_C}\underline A_C\cong G$ naturally, so tensoring with it is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Apply the open-closed flatness criterion [lem-sfb-open-closed-flatness] to $a$ in each topology: its final clause states that $a_*M$ is flat whenever $M$ is a flat $\underline A_C$-module sheaf; in the pro-etale case its quasi-compact-open hypothesis is the one in the statement. Flatness is invariant under isomorphism, so by the identifications of step 1 both support quotients $Q^{\tau}_{T,C}\cong a_*\underline A_C$ are flat. Each quotient placed in degree zero is a bounded-above complex whose terms are flat, so it is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site].

source.place: support quotient flatness and degree-zero K-flatness

proof.text: For an etale geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$, use that a closed immersion is finite and that finite direct-image stalks are the product of the stalks over the geometric fibre. The fibre of $a$ over $\bar t$ is empty when $\bar t$ lies in $T\setminus C$ and consists of the unique corresponding geometric point of $C$ when it lies on $C$. The constant-sheaf stalk lemma identifies the stalk of $A_C$ at that point with $A$; thus the stalk of $a_*A_C$, and hence of $Q^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}$, is canonically $0$ off $C$ and $A$ on $C$. The identification in Step 1 carries the quotient generator through the unit, so it maps to $1$ on the latter stalk.

proof.text:
Let $V$ be $T$ or $U=T\setminus C$, an open object of both $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and write $F^	au_V=j_{V!}\underline A_V$; for $V=T$ this is $\underline A_T$, since every object has exactly one map to the final object. As in step 1, the free-Yoneda bijection [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] and the universal property of sheafification, applied to the presheaves of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and [def-weil-extension-by-zero], give bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(F^	au_V,N)\cong N(V)$, $f\mapsto f(e_V)$, natural in the module sheaf $N$; precomposition with the defining arrow $\iota^	au:F^	au_U	o F^	au_T$ is restriction $N(T)	o N(U)$. For a pro-etale $A$-module sheaf $N$, the module adjunction $
u_T^*\dashv
u_{T,*}$ of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and $(
u_{T,*}N)(V)=N(V)$ give bijections, natural in $N$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(
u_T^*F^{\mathrm{et}}_V,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F^{\mathrm{et}}_V,
u_{T,*}N)\cong N(V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F^{\mathrm{proet}}_V,N).$$
By Yoneda they come from a unique isomorphism $\varphi_V:
u_T^*F^{\mathrm{et}}_V\xrightarrow{\sim}F^{\mathrm{proet}}_V$, the one sending the pulled-back generator to the generator; for $V=T$ it sends $
u_T^*1$ to $1$ and so is the ring identification of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact](1). By naturality of the adjunction, precomposition with $
u_T^*\iota^{\mathrm{et}}$ is also restriction $N(T)	o N(U)$, hence $\varphi_T\circ
u_T^*\iota^{\mathrm{et}}=\iota^{\mathrm{proet}}\circ\varphi_U$. The functor $
u_T^*$ is exact by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact](2), so $
u_T^*r^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}$ is a cokernel of $
u_T^*\iota^{\mathrm{et}}$. Therefore $\varphi_T$ induces an isomorphism $\psi:
u_T^*Q^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}\xrightarrow{\sim}Q^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}$ with $\psi\circ
u_T^*r^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}=r^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}\circ\varphi_T$, and it is the only such map because $
u_T^*r^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}$ is an epimorphism. This is the asserted canonical comparison.
